title: The Moon Tarot Card Meaning: Upright, Reversed & Love
description: The Moon upright: uncertainty, intuition; reversed: confusion lifting. Love, work, advice, Waite's 1911 text and the 1909 card. Draw it for your question.
image_alt: The Moon, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: a yellow moon with a face in profile shines between two gray towers; a dog and a wolf look up at it, and a crayfish climbs out of a pool.
capsule: The Moon is card XVIII of the Major Arcana: uncertainty, intuition and dreams. Reversed, the haze starts to lift, or worry runs ahead of the facts. It is a dim card, not a dark one, and it asks for patience. As a yes or no, it says not clear yet, since the path is only half lit.

blocks.heading: What is on The Moon card?
paragraphs: A large moon fills the top of the card, with a face drawn in profile inside it. Waite says it "is increasing on what is called the side of mercy, to the right of the observer" and has "sixteen chief and sixteen secondary rays" (p. 140). On the 1909 card the moon is yellow, the face has its eyes closed, small yellow drops fall from it, and XVIII stands above.

Below are two gray towers, and between them a path runs from the water up into distant hills. Waite calls it "the issue into the unknown" (p. 140). A dog and a wolf sit on the grass, heads raised; for Waite they are "the fears of the natural mind" facing that way out, "when there is only reflected light to guide it" (p. 140). On the 1909 card the dog is orange and the wolf a pale yellow.

In the foreground a crayfish climbs out of a pool. Waite describes something that comes "up out of the deeps" and tries to reach the land, but "as a rule it sinks back whence it came" (pp. 140, 143). Over all of this, he writes, "The face of the mind directs a calm gaze upon the unrest below", and the message of the card is "Peace, be still" (p. 143).

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about The Moon?
paragraphs: Put plainly, the upright list gathers what cannot be seen well: things kept out of view, mistakes, being misled. The reversed list is milder: unsteadiness, changeable moods, silence, smaller errors. Arcana Diary reads those darker upright words only as uncertainty, a stretch when it is easy to misread what you see.

Waite's own view of the card is quieter. He saw in it "life of the imagination apart from life of the spirit", and wrote that "The intellectual light is a reflection" (p. 140). In his reading, the dim light on the card belongs to the mind itself.

blocks.heading: What does The Moon mean upright?
paragraphs: Upright, The Moon points to uncertainty: a stretch when things are not fully visible yet, and feelings, hints and half-formed worries blur together. It often shows up while you are waiting for information, or when your mind fills the gaps with guesses.

The card also honors intuition and dreams. They are good at shaping questions (what am I sensing? what keeps coming back?) and less reliable as conclusions. The path on the card is real; it is just lit by a softer light than you would like.
If this sounds like your situation, move slowly and check what is real before acting. Hidden feelings, your own included, may be part of the picture. What are you feeling that you have not named yet?

blocks.heading: What does The Moon mean reversed?
paragraphs: Reversed, The Moon can point to confusion lifting: something you avoided looking at becomes easier to see, and the fog thins. It can also mean worry running ahead of the facts, when the mind fills the dark with more than is there.

Waite's reversed list speaks of instability and "lesser degrees of deception and error" (p. 286), which sits close to the first reading: the haze is still there, only thinner. Worry outrunning the facts is today's reading rather than Waite's.
Either way, clearer sight comes from separating two lists: what you know and what you only imagine. Let the second list wait for better light.

blocks.heading: What does The Moon mean in love?
paragraphs: In love, The Moon asks for patience with mixed signals. If you have no partner right now, it can point to attraction mixed with uncertainty, or to daydreams about someone that are still mostly your own imagining.

Within a relationship, it can describe a stretch when things feel unclear between you. The card stays with your side: notice what you feel, ask openly instead of guessing, and give trust time to grow.
Turned upside down in love, it may show a misunderstanding clearing, or worry building stories faster than facts. What do you actually know, and what have you only assumed?

blocks.heading: What does The Moon mean for work and money?
paragraphs: At work, The Moon can point to unclear information: plans still taking shape, instructions open to interpretation, a situation you cannot quite read yet. It favors asking questions and writing things down over acting on assumptions.
In money matters, examine how you decide: from facts, or from a vague hope or a vague worry? Clarity first, choices second.
Reversed, notice where a confusing matter at work is starting to clear, and use that moment to confirm the details.

blocks.heading: What is The Moon's advice?
paragraphs: Wait for clearer light: write down what you know and what you only fear. The Moon's advice is to keep those two lists apart and act only on the first. Read them again later and see which one has changed.

blocks.heading: Is The Moon a yes or no card?
The Moon as a person and as a feeling
paragraphs: In a spread, The Moon can stand for someone hard to read, or for a role that is still forming and keeps changing shape. Turned toward you, it marks the dreamer in you, the part that senses more than it can explain. Emotionally it is like walking at night, unease mixed with intuition; reversed, it is the relief of first light, or a worry that keeps circling.

pairs.text: Uncertainty giving way to clarity. Wait for daylight before you decide.
A choice made harder by poor visibility. Gather one more fact before you pick a side.
Worries that grow in the dark. Write them down; on paper they often look smaller.
Walking away by moonlight. Make sure you know what you are leaving, and why.

blocks.heading: The Moon or The High Priestess?
paragraphs: Both cards deal with what is not fully in view. In Waite's description of the High Priestess, a crescent moon lies at her feet and her mantle half hides a scroll, so that part of its teaching is said and part only hinted (p. 76); her modern sense is intuition and inner knowing, calm and still. The Moon is the restless version: a path at night, animals calling, shapes hard to make out. The High Priestess knows quietly; The Moon is still finding out.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about The Moon
paragraphs: What do I actually know about this, and what am I only guessing?
Which feeling have I been keeping out of sight, even from myself?
What would I ask if I let intuition shape the question rather than the answer?

faq.q: Is The Moon a good or bad card?
faq.a: Neither, really. It is a card of low visibility: not a sign that something is wrong, only that the full picture is not in view yet. It supports patience, imagination and listening to hunches. Its caution is against treating a guess as if it were a fact.

faq.q: Does The Moon mean someone is lying to me?
faq.a: Cards on this site are not read for another person's intentions. Waite's old list does include deception (p. 286), but here the card points to your side: information you are missing, or an assumption you are leaning on. A calm, direct question usually helps more than suspicion.

faq.q: What are the drops falling from the moon?
faq.a: Waite calls them dew. In Part I he notes that in nearly all versions the moon is "shedding the moisture of fertilizing dew in great drops" (p. 27). In the card's own entry he adds that "the dew of thought falls" (p. 143) while the mind looks down without alarm at the restless creatures below.

faq.q: Is The Moon a sign to trust my intuition?
faq.a: Partly. The card values intuition, but it also shows how easily shapes are misread at night. Use your hunches to choose what to look into, then compare them with what you can confirm in daylight. Intuition is the lantern here, not the map.
